content.value_statement: Complex agent work can fail when one context window carries every task. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code design agent systems with clear handoffs.
actual_capabilities: Explains supervisor, swarm, and hierarchical architecture patterns for agent systems.
Compares context isolation methods, including full delegation, instruction passing, and shared file memory.
Provides guidance for handoffs, weighted voting, debate protocols, checkpointing, and failure handling.
Includes framework-oriented examples for LangGraph, AutoGen, and CrewAI-style implementations.
Supplies a Python helper for messaging, handoffs, consensus, and circuit breaker utilities.
limitations: Does not provide a complete production framework or deployable service.
Example code needs adaptation before use with real agents, permissions, and data stores.
Does not replace security review for tools that write files, browse the web, or execute actions.
Framework examples may need updates as LangGraph, AutoGen, and CrewAI APIs change.

use_cases.title: Plan Agent Workflows
use_cases.description: Design clear agent roles, routing paths, and handoff points for a complex application.

use_cases.title: Review Architecture Choices
use_cases.description: Compare supervisor, swarm, and hierarchy patterns before committing to an implementation.

use_cases.title: Prototype Coordination Logic
use_cases.description: Use the helper patterns to model messaging, consensus, and recovery before production integration.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Pattern
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new agent workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use multi-agent-patterns to recommend one architecture for [task]. Explain the pattern, agent roles, handoff points, and main risks.

prompt_templates.title: Design Handoffs
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate design for routing between specialized agents.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use multi-agent-patterns to design handoff protocols for [workflow]. Include state passed, ownership changes, validation checks, and stop conditions.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Consensus
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of decision quality in a multi-agent system.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use multi-agent-patterns to assess consensus for [decision process]. Compare voting, debate, confidence weighting, and failure risks.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Production Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Use multi-agent-patterns to audit [architecture]. Identify bottlenecks, context leaks, retry loops, checkpoint needs, and monitoring signals.

output_examples.input: Design an agent team for research, analysis, and report writing.
output_examples.output: A supervisor-led workflow with researcher, analyst, and writer agents, plus direct pass-through for final specialist responses.

output_examples.input: Compare swarm and supervisor patterns for customer support routing.
output_examples.output: A tradeoff summary covering control, flexibility, divergence risk, escalation paths, and when each pattern fits.

output_examples.input: Find failure modes in a proposed multi-agent workflow.
output_examples.output: A review of supervisor bottlenecks, context leakage, weak consensus, missing checkpoints, and retry or circuit breaker gaps.

best_practices: Use multi-agent designs when context isolation or parallel work is clearly needed.
Define explicit handoff payloads, stop conditions, and validation checks before implementation.
Test failure paths, retry behavior, and consensus quality with realistic tasks.
anti_patterns: Splitting work into agents only to mimic a team structure.
Letting every agent see all context when isolation is the main goal.
Using majority voting without confidence, expertise, or critique safeguards.

faq.question: What does this skill help me design?
faq.answer: It helps design multi-agent systems with supervisors, swarms, hierarchies, handoffs, consensus, and recovery patterns.

faq.question: Does it include runnable code?
faq.answer: It includes examples and a Python coordination helper. Production use still needs integration, tests, and permission controls.

faq.question: When should I avoid a multi-agent design?
faq.answer: Avoid it when one agent can solve the task without context pressure, parallel work, or specialized tools.

faq.question: Which frameworks are discussed?
faq.answer: The reference material discusses LangGraph, AutoGen, and CrewAI-style patterns.

faq.question: Can it help with failure handling?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers bottlenecks, divergence, error propagation, checkpointing, retries, and circuit breaker concepts.

faq.question: Is it specific to Claude or Codex?
faq.answer: No. The concepts apply broadly, with marketplace support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code users.
